get.summary: Run the match analysis over Server-Sent Events.
get.description: The same three-stage chain as `POST /jobs/{slug}/match-analysis`, streamed as SSE (`text/event-stream`) rather than a single JSON body. Each event’s `kind` is one of `stage_start`, `stage_done`, `thinking`, `requirements`, `dimensions`, `final`; the `final` event carries the completed `analysis` (the same shape as the match-analysis endpoints). Not a JSON endpoint.

get.summary: A company and a page of its open jobs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size for the jobs list.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip in the jobs list.

get.summary: A company’s closed postings — the company page’s Closed tab.
get.description: A page of the postings the company has closed, most recently closed first. Closed postings are not in search, so this is the only list of them. There is no total: `meta.has_more` says whether another page follows. Paging reaches the first 2000 rows (`offset + limit` ≤ 2000); a deeper page is a `400`. An unknown slug is a `404`; a slug retired by a company merge redirects `301` to the canonical one.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip; `offset + limit` may not exceed 2000.

get.summary: How one company hires over time — the company page’s Hiring tab.
get.description: The company’s postings added vs. removed per period (dense, missing periods are 0, same window rules as `/stats/jobs-activity`), its open postings now and 30 days ago, and the median days its postings stay open before an employer-side closure over the last 180 days, and the page views its postings drew over the last 30 days and the 30 before (`views`, `views_prev`: one visitor counted once per posting per day, crawlers excluded). `lifetime` is omitted below 5 such closures — absent, never 0. An unknown slug is a `404`; a slug retired by a company merge redirects `301` to the canonical one.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start date (UTC). Defaults to a per-granularity window before `to`.

post.summary: Create an account and start a session.
Sign in and start a session.

get.description: Browser-only: redirects to the provider, then back to `/auth/oauth/{provider}/callback`, which sets the session cookie and redirects to the app. Not a JSON endpoint.

post.summary: Sign out every session on the account, including this one.
post.description: Bumps the account’s session generation (stranding every issued token and API-key session state) then clears the caller’s cookie. Cookie-only — an API key must not be able to sign a human out of their browser. Returns `204 No Content`.

post.summary: Redeem a mobile OAuth callback code for a session.
post.description: Mobile-only: the app’s custom-scheme OAuth callback carries a single-use code (not the session directly); this exchanges it for the session cookie, landing in the app’s own cookie jar. Public — the code is the credential, and a missing/expired/reused one is a `401`.

code.description: The one-time code from the mobile callback redirect.

get.summary: Consent screen for "Sign in with freehire" from the browser extension.
get.description: Opened by the extension via `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow`, not called directly — renders an HTML consent page, not JSON. `redirect_uri` must be an allowlisted `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org` origin, or this is a `400`. A signed-out visitor is bounced through sign-in first, then back to this same consent step.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: The allowlisted chromiumapp.org redirect the extension is listening on.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value echoed back on completion.

post.summary: Submit the consent decision and mint the extension’s session token.
post.description: Submitted by the consent screen’s own form, not called directly. On `decision=allow`, 302-redirects to `redirect_uri` with a session token in the URL fragment (never the query, so it is never logged or sent to a server); on anything else, redirects with `error=access_denied`. Not a JSON endpoint.

redirect_uri.description: Must match the allowlisted redirect validated on the GET step.

get.summary: A batch of open jobs for the swipe triage deck.
get.description: Runs the same query as search (same facets, `q`, and sort), then excludes the jobs you have already saved or dismissed. A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused, and listed in `meta.ignored_params`, exactly as in search. `503` when search is unavailable.

post.summary: Send a message and stream the turn as Server-Sent Events.
post.description: Body is `{"text": "..."}` (max ~8000 characters, deployment-configured). The response is `text/event-stream`, not JSON: each frame is `event: <kind>` plus a `data:` line carrying the JSON event (whose own `type` field repeats the kind). Kinds: `queued` (this turn waited for one already running), `user_prompt`, `assistant_text` / `assistant_thought` (streamed deltas), `tool_use` / `tool_result`, `usage`, and exactly one terminal `result` carrying `stop_reason` (`completed`, `cancelled`, or `error`). The turn keeps running even if you stop reading — stopping it is a separate call to `.../cancel`.

text.example: Should I relocate for this role?

post.summary: Have the assistant speak first, on an `interview`/`debrief` session.
post.description: Streams one turn under a server-side brief (no body), the same SSE shape as `.../messages`. `409` if the session’s preset does not open by itself, or if it already has an assistant message (an opening cannot be re-run).

post.summary: Catch an `apply` session up on its automatic application.
post.description: When the application has events the conversation has not narrated, streams one turn telling the candidate what changed (no body), the same SSE shape as `.../messages`; otherwise `204` and nothing runs. Not charged to the assistant-message allowance. A turn that fails is narrated again on the next call. `409` for a session that is not an `apply` conversation.

post.summary: Resume after a failed turn, without adding another user message.
post.description: Re-runs the loop over the existing history (no body) — the same SSE shape as `.../messages`. `409 "nothing to retry"` when the session has no prior user message.

post.summary: Run an unattended CV-tailoring pass as one long streamed turn.
post.description: Session-only, not API-key — an unattended run edits a CV, and the browser is the only place you can watch it happen and undo it. Requires a `tailor` session bound to both a CV and a vacancy (`409` otherwise). Same SSE shape as `.../messages`, no body; every edit lands in one revision batch, so undoing the run is reverting that batch.

post.summary: Extract a structured profile from an uploaded résumé (no LLM).
post.description: Accepts a PDF (`multipart/form-data` field `file`) or plain text (`application/json` `{ "text": ... }`). Returns canonical skill slugs, the categories it spans, and the resolved seniority (omitted when unresolved). When storage is configured it also stores the résumé once.

text.description: Résumé plain text (JSON path); or send a PDF as multipart field `file`.

put.description: Accepts a PDF (multipart `file`) or JSON `{ "text": ... }`. Returns the résumé metadata. `501` when object storage is unconfigured.

text.description: Résumé plain text (JSON path); or send a PDF as multipart field `file`.

get.summary: Your Discord link status, and whether the paid role is on it.

delete.summary: Unlink your Discord account, giving up the paid role with it.

get.summary: Your webhook destination for saved-search matches, or null if none is configured.

post.summary: Create your webhook destination, or update its URL if one already exists.
post.description: There is exactly one destination per account. Deliveries are plain, unsigned HTTP POSTs — subscribe a saved search to the `webhook` channel (see `POST /me/subscriptions`) to receive its matches here. Before the URL is stored it receives a test delivery (`saved_search_name` "freehire webhook test", an empty `jobs` list); a URL that does not answer it with a 2xx is refused with 422, naming what it answered.

url.description: Destination URL — must be http or https.

patch.summary: Enable or disable your webhook destination without changing its URL.

post.summary: Send a test delivery to your stored webhook destination.
post.description: The same sample delivery saving a URL sends. A 2xx answer stamps `last_success_at` and returns the destination; anything else is a 422 naming what the destination answered, and changes nothing. 404 when no destination is configured.
Revokes every session; your own cookie is re-issued at the new generation, so you stay signed in and everyone else is signed out.

delete.summary: Delete your account and everything under it.

get.summary: The same document as server-sent events, one per sample.
get.description: A `progress` event carrying the full document on connect and after every 15-second sample, with a `ping` event between to keep idle connections alive.

post.summary: Offer to refer into a company. Multipart — proof required.
post.description: The proof (an offer letter, badge, anything showing you work there) is stored privately and shown only to a moderator; its storage key is never exposed on the wire. The offer is pending until decided.

company_slug.description: The company you can refer into.

linkedin_url.description: Your profile, for the moderator to check against.

get.summary: View the candidate's CV for one incoming request.

get.description: Answers 501 on a deployment with no typst binary configured; everything else still works.

put.description: Multipart upload of the `file` part — JPEG, PNG, or WebP, capped at 8 MB and replaces any existing headshot. `501` when object storage is not configured, `400` for an undecodable, unsupported, or oversized image.

get.summary: Whether you have a stored headshot, and when it was uploaded.
get.description: `enabled` is false when object storage is not configured — the client should then offer no upload control at all rather than one that answers `501`. `uploaded_at` doubles as a cache-busting value for the image URL.

get.summary: The stored headshot itself, as image bytes.
get.description: Not a JSON endpoint — the response is `image/jpeg` with a short private cache lifetime (60s), meant to be busted with `?v=<uploaded_at>`. `404` when no headshot is stored.

post.summary: Transcribe one short audio recording to text.
post.description: Multipart upload of the `file` part — webm, mp4, m4a, ogg, wav, or mp3, capped at ~8 minutes of audio (2 MB). `501` when no speech gateway is configured, `502` if the gateway call itself fails, `400` for an empty recording.
